newsitem.title: USA: Enron, Portland General get accord.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Portland General get accord.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Corp said on Tuesday they had completed a settlement agreement with the staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission on their proposed $2.1 billion merger.
They said the agreement would now be presented to the three-member commission for its approval.
Under the proposed merger agreement, the two companies said they would guarantee a $141 million rate decrease to Portland General's retail electricity customers.
The Oregon commission had recommended against the merger unless the companies came up with rate reductions for Portland General's electricity customers.
"We are now confident that we have an agreement the commissioners will be able to approve," Enron chairman Ken Lay said in a statement.
Portland General shareholders are scheduled to vote to approve the merger on June 24. Under the deal they would receive Enron stock for their Portland General holdings.
